Since the issue involved in the aforesaid Petitions is identical and which fact is not disputed by the learned counsel for the 8-31wp9570-25g.doc Respondents, all the aforesaid Petitions are being disposed of by a common order.

2. By these Petitions, the Petitioners seek payment of 30% solatium, 12% of the component and requisite amount of interest in saddition to the market value of the land as provided for under the Land Acquisition Act / Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
3.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Reliance is placed by both, the learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned counsel for the Respondents on the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Union of India vs. Tarsem, Singh & Ors.

entities.text: Union of India vs. Tarsem, Singh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
reported in (2019) 9 SCC 304.
4. Learned counsel for the Respondents does not dispute that the decision in Tarsem Singh (supra)
applies to all the Petitioners in the aforesaid Petitions.

He further states that the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) has filed a Review Petition seeking review of of Tarsem's decision and that the said Review Petition is pending before the Supreme Court.

6 5. Considering the aforesaid, since the Petitioners are squarely covered by the judgment of the Apex Court in Tarsem Singh (supra), 8-31wp9570-25g.doc we direct the Petitioners to furnish the copy of the award to NHAI within a period of one week from the date of uploading of this order to facilitate the NHAI to compute the solatium and interest in accordance with law.

6. We further direct that the NHAI shall thereafter, compute solatium and interest, in accordance with the principle of law as laid down in the case of Tarsem Singh (supra) within three months from the date on which the Petitioners furnish a copy of the award to the NHAI.
7. The computed amount shall thereafter be deposited by the NHAI with the Collector of the concerned Districts, within one week i.e. after computing the solatium and interest.

8. Since the NHAI has filed a Review Petition seeking review of Tarsem Singh's (supra) decision before the Supreme Court and the same is pending, we direct the Collector not to disburse the said amount to the respective Petitioners.

9. Needless to state, that the disbursement will be subject to the out come of the Review Petition.
Learned AGPs appearing for the Collector submit that in the event the Review Petition filed by the the 8-31wp9570-25g.doc NHAI is dismissed, the concerned Collector will forthwith start disbursing the said amount to the Petitioners.
Statement made by the respective AGPs is accepted.
10. The aforesaid Petitions stand disposed of on the aforesaid terms.
11. List the aforesaid Petition for reporting compliance of the order on 17th December, 2025.

(SANDESH D. PATIL, J.) (REVATI MOHITE DERE, J.)
